source.original_title: 05/01/2026 - Bryant Fields & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/01/2026 - Bryant Fields & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

prospect.name: Bryant Fields
prospect.occupation: Commercialisation of clinical trial analytics products and services
prospect.training_background: Endurance athlete — marathons (3 planned this year), returning to triathlon, running 25-30 miles/week across 3-4 sessions; has a run coach; previously had an in-person personal trainer for traditional weightlifting; used a remote coach during the pandemic; currently in physical therapy 3 days/week
prospect.medical: Meniscus tear and surgery 2021/2022; quad tendonitis; quad tear; rotator cuff / shoulder injury sustained during a resistance band movement last year; currently in active physical therapy and doing prescribed PT routines

signals: Repeated injury sequence over 3-4 years that cost him athletic capacity: 'it's just been one thing after another'
Wants a former self back: 'I want to be athletic again', 'I'm just trying to turn the clock back'
Regret marker — expensive suits upstairs with tags still on that no longer fit
Not price-insensitive, which rules out the_optimizer: 'that's out of my range'

goals.text: Build lean muscle mass and improve body composition / lose body fat
Fit back into the expensive suits still hanging upstairs with tags on
Improve marathon performance — from just finishing toward a 4:30, then 4:15, eventually sub-4
Improve mobility and functional movement rather than static weightlifting
Shift from a rehab state to a prehab state so injuries stop recurring
Long-term independence and quality of life — lift his own suitcase into the overhead bin, walk to the gate on his own
Regain confidence in his body's ability to perform

pains.text: Chain of injuries over the last three to four years — meniscus tear and surgery, quad tendonitis, quad tear, rotator cuff — that repeatedly reset his progress
Lost his in-person trainer when the trainer left for the state trooper academy and has not trained consistently since; December to February on his own
Knows he is taking too many days off and is operating below his own standard: 'I'm not' operating at 100%
Conflicting kettlebell technique advice online — 'you look at one post, you look at one person, oh you got to do it this way, you got to do it that way'
Existing run coach only programmes running; nothing addresses lean mass, which he has been attempting alone
Lack of confidence in his body to hit performance targets — 'I don't have the confidence in my body that I can do those things'
Prior remote coaching during the pandemic felt materially worse than in-person

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, that's way out of my expectation.
objections.rep_response: Did not isolate the objection or run any part of the money play; said 'Sure. All good, man. All good' and asked whether he had any questions

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, that's out of my range.
objections.rep_response: Did not explore financials; moved the conversation onto the $200/mo Primal University product

objections.raw_quote: I do think there is a different dynamic when it's in-person versus remote.
objections.rep_response: Asked why he was considering the virtual route at all given that experience; accepted the answer and did not reframe how the video feedback loop closes the in-person gap

objections.raw_quote: I'm going to, I guess, think about it.
objections.rep_response: Later asked 'what do you need to go over before making that decision?' — one probe only, no further play

objections.raw_quote: I'm three weeks out from my next marathon. So if I were to commit now, I don't know how this would fit in... three weeks out from a marathon, I'm not doing anything different.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the timing constraint without challenge and offered to message him at the three-week mark

offer.guarantee_mentioned: On the $1,200 one-month tier: 'If you love it, you just pay the differential to the three or the six or the 12. If not, we just part ways and shake hands as friends.' Separately: 'we don't even hold you for the one-on-one coaching... We provide you with graceful exits on both.'

evidence: Rep proposed and prospect agreed to a re-contact after his marathon: 'would it make sense to potentially revisit this and have myself message you around that three-week mark' — 'yeah yeah yeah let's do that'
Prospect said he would think about the $200/mo Primal University option and revisit at the end of the month

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: the core one-on-one offer was explicitly rejected twice on price — 'that's way out of my expectation' and 'that's out of my range' — so on the coaching programme itself this is effectively lost
COUNTER-EVIDENCE: prospect stated he will not change anything three weeks out from a marathon, so no decision was available on this call
outcome.next_step: Rep to message the prospect in approximately three weeks, after his Cape Town marathon; prospect to consider Primal University at $200/mo

notable.note: Prospect disclosed an active physical therapy course and a four-injury history (meniscus surgery, quad tendonitis, quad tear, rotator cuff) and the rep never asked whether a clinician had cleared kettlebell work — he instead recommended the unsupervised self-paced product as possibly 'a better fit'. Separately the rep quoted two tiers that are not in the sanctioned price list ($1,200 for one month, $4,000 for three months) and made an unqualified cancellation representation on the 6- and 12-month coaching. On process, the entire Consequence Frame phase was skipped and the money objection was met with an immediate downsell rather than the scripted open-wallet play.

quality.notes: Extensive and sustained label inversion. Rep lines are frequently attributed to 'BPF' — e.g. 'So, Brian, we have a limited amount of time. Should we hop into it?' and 'Brian, you have a pen, paper, laptop, iPad?' are both labelled BPF but are unmistakably the rep. Prospect answers are likewise attributed to Farooq Bey. Roles were resolved from content throughout; no line-level attribution should be trusted in this file.
